title: fix: parse {;var} before a literal starting with '='
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #3852.

`_scan_prefix` in `src/mcp/shared/uri_template.py` took the empty-value reading whenever the URI at the name's position began with the following literal, and it did that before checking for the `=` separator. When the literal itself starts with `=`, that test fires on the separator, so the value is read as empty and the literal text is pushed into the greedy variable.

Measured on `77001c9`, for template `{;a}=end{+rest}` with `a="end", rest="/x"`:

| stage | value |
| --- | --- |
| `expand()` | `;a=end=end/x` |
| `match()` before | `{'a': '', 'rest': '=end/x'}` |
| `match()` after | `{'a': 'end', 'rest': '/x'}` |

So `match(expand(vars)) != vars` for that case. The narrow failing set matches what was measured in the issue thread: `a=""` and `a="x"` already round-trip, and so does `/api{;mode}=fast{/id}`.

## The fix

In the `ifemp` branch, when `uri[pos] == "="`, try the `;name=value` reading first, bounded to the next literal, then fall back to the empty reading.

The bounded span is the part that matters. Taking the stop-char span for the value captures `end=end` from `;a=end=end/x`, because `=` does not end a `;` value, and the following `=end` literal then fails and falls back to the reading that is wrong today. Finding the next literal instead gives `end`, which round-trips.

## Ambiguity, stated rather than hidden

`;a=end=end/x` is genuinely ambiguous for `{;a}=end{+rest}`: both `{a: "end", rest: "/x"}` and `{a: "", rest: "=end/x"}` expand to it. The value reading wins here, for consistency with the suffix scan, which already prefers `;name=value` for `{;a}=end{/rest}`. A test names that trade explicitly so a later change cannot flip it silently.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/shared/test_uri_template.py` -> 317 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/shared/ tests/issues/ tests/docs_src/test_uri_templates.py` -> 1047 passed, 1 skipped
- The three added tests fail on unpatched `77001c9` and pass with this patch, so they are regression tests and not just descriptions
- `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` clean on both changed files

Full test suite was not run, only the suites that touch `uri_template` plus the shared and issues trees.

title: Record tool error results on the client OpenTelemetry span
body:
<!--
Pull requests from outside the maintainer team need to link an open issue that
a maintainer has assigned to you (or one labeled `help wanted`); others are
closed automatically until that's in place. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.
-->

Fixes #3810

<!-- Provide a brief summary of your changes -->
Records tool error results on the client OpenTelemetry span when `CallToolResult.isError` is `True`.

## Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change needed? What problem does it solve? -->
In MCP, application-level tool errors return a successful JSON-RPC response containing `isError=True` in the result payload rather than a JSON-RPC `ErrorData` protocol error. Previously, `send_raw_request` only checked if `outcome` was an `ErrorData` instance to record errors on the client OpenTelemetry span. Consequently, when a tool execution failed with `CallToolResult.isError=True`, the client span remained with `StatusCode.UNSET` and no error attributes, diverging from server spans which record `StatusCode.ERROR` and `error.type="tool_error"`.

This change updates `send_raw_request` in `src/mcp/shared/jsonrpc_dispatcher.py` to check for `method == "tools/call"` with `outcome.get("isError") is True`. When encountered, the client span is marked with `span.set_status(StatusCode.ERROR)` and `span.set_attribute("error.type", "tool_error")`, adhering to OpenTelemetry GenAI MCP semantic conventions without setting `rpc.response.status_code`.

## How Has This Been Tested?
<!-- Have you tested this in a real application? Which scenarios were tested? -->
Added unit test `test_client_and_server_spans_agree_on_tool_error` in `tests/shared/test_otel.py`:
- Configured an `MCPServer` with an `ok` tool (returning `"fine"`) and a `fail` tool (raising `ToolError("upstream unavailable")`).
- Invoked both tools via `Client(server, mode="legacy")` and inspected spans captured via Logfire (`CaptureLogfire`).
- Verified that the successful tool call leaves both client and server spans in `StatusCode.UNSET` with no `error.type`.
- Verified that the failed tool call marks both client and server spans with `StatusCode.ERROR` and `error.type="tool_error"`.
- Verified that both spans share the same `trace_id` and that `rpc.response.status_code` is not set on the client span.

## Breaking Changes
<!-- Will users need to update their code or configurations? -->
None. This change only updates OpenTelemetry client span status and attributes for failed tool calls.

title: Updates to conform to section 3.1 of the OAuth 2.1 specification
body:
<!--
Pull requests from outside the maintainer team need to link an open issue that
a maintainer has assigned to you (or one labeled `help wanted`); others are
closed automatically until that's in place. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.
-->

Fixes #3856 and #2776 

<!-- Provide a brief summary of your changes -->
Added some helper functions in src/mcp/shared/auth_utils.py to add, remove and replace query params to a URL and then used those in src/mcp/client/auth/oauth2.py in _perform_authorization_code_grant to conform to the rules in section 3.1 of the OAuth 2.1 spec.
There is one change to check if a fragment has been added to the authorization_url and if so to reject it. You could also make an argument to accept the URL and strip the fragment rather than to return an error
It then later when adding query params to the url calls the new function replace_query_params to append the params to the url without interfering with any existing query params and also validates that the URL doesn't already contain any of the params used by the authorization request.

Devin AI was used to document the code changes and to update the tests to cover the changes.

## Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change needed? What problem does it solve? -->
Not accepting (or removing fragments) from the authorization_url can help protect against fragment extension attacks, and validating that the authorization URL doesn't already contain parameters expected to be added by the request generation prevents attacks where the param provided with the authorization_url is used instead of the params added by the MCP client.

## How Has This Been Tested?
It has been tested against a proprietary OAuth 2.1 authorization server which expects certain query params in the authorization_url obtained via OpenId Discovery are retained.

Users should not have to update anything

title: docs(client): complete the Args blocks in ClientSession
body:
Fixes #3846

---

Four `ClientSession` methods document only their input-required kwargs, so the rendered reference hides the arguments a caller has to pass. The block was written once for the newer kwargs and copied to the neighbours.

| Method | Documented | Added |
|---|---|---|
| `send_request` | `metadata` | `request`, `result_type`, `request_read_timeout_seconds`, `progress_callback` |
| `read_resource` | 3 kwargs | `uri` (the only parameter without a default), `meta` |
| `call_tool` | 4 kwargs | `name`, `arguments`, `read_timeout_seconds`, `progress_callback`, `meta` |
| `get_prompt` | 3 kwargs | `name`, `arguments`, `meta` |

**On the overload question raised in the issue:** `mkdocs.yml` sets no `show_overloads` option, so mkdocstrings renders the overload signatures and takes the docstring from the implementation — the blocks belong on the implementation, which is where they are. I did not add Args blocks to the `@overload` stubs; that would duplicate four copies of the same text.

**Verification**

- AST comparison against the previous head with docstrings excluded: identical, so only the docstrings changed.
- Every parameter of the four methods now appears in its `Args:` block (checked by parsing the module with `ast`).
- `pytest tests/client/test_session.py` → **94 passed**.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the file: pass.

Credit to media-ctrl for reproducing this on `main` and for widening the scope from four methods to the surrounding copies.

I did not add the "walk the public client methods and assert every parameter appears in Args" test suggested in the issue — that is a behaviour change for the test suite and worth its own PR if you want it. Say so and I will open it.

title: fix(server): return a descriptive error for requests before initialization
body:
Fixes #423.

### Problem

When a client sends a request (e.g. `tools/list`) before completing the
`initialize` handshake — the common case after a server restart or a
dropped SSE connection, when the client reuses a stale session — the v2
server answers with `-32602 "Invalid request parameters"` and empty
`data`. That is indistinguishable from a real parameter-validation
failure, so debugging starts at the wrong layer (reported by @Luxian on
the issue; the same complaint behind the original crash report).

The pre-v2 fix (PR #2411) was closed unmerged because the v2 rework
changed the code it targeted; the maintainer (@maxisbey, 2026-08-10)
invited reopening it if still relevant against v2. It is: the crash is
gone, but the misleading error remains.

### Solution

In `ServerRunner._on_request` (`src/mcp/server/runner.py`), when the
method is known but initialization has not been accepted, raise
`MCPError(code=INVALID_REQUEST, message="Received request before
initialization was complete", data="The client must send an 'initialize'
request before any other request.")` instead of the generic
`INVALID_PARAMS` error — so the client learns it must (re-)run
`initialize` first. This follows #2411's approach (INVALID_REQUEST +
the original v1 message), re-implemented for the v2 runner.

Untouched on purpose:

- `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` for unknown methods (probing clients key off
  `-32601` in every initialization state).
- The `ping` exemption (`_INIT_EXEMPT`).
- Genuine parameter-validation failures, which stay `-32602`
  (`test_runner_malformed_params_...`, `test_wire.py`, otel tests).

### Tests

- `tests/server/test_runner.py`: updated the three init-gate assertions
  (`test_runner_gates_requests_before_initialize`,
  `test_runner_custom_method_with_handler_is_still_gated_before_initialize`,
  middleware-rejection test) to the new error shape.
- `tests/interaction/lowlevel/test_initialize.py`:
  `test_request_before_initialization_is_rejected` — snapshot regenerated
  with `--inline-snapshot=fix`; docstring updated (it previously recorded
  the generic-error gap as a known deficiency).

### Verification (local, 2026-11-08)

- Baseline before the change: 139 passed
  (`test_runner.py` + `test_initialize.py`).
- After the change: 233 passed across the five related files
  (`test_runner.py`, `test_initialize.py`, `test_wire.py`,
  `test_streamable_http_modern.py`, `test_otel.py`).
- `ruff format --check` + `ruff check`: clean. `pyright
  src/mcp/server/runner.py`: 0 errors.
- Full `./scripts/test`: 6,221 passed, 12 failed (273s). The 12 failures
  are PRE-EXISTING and environmental, not from this change — verified by
  re-running the same 13 tests on the clean tree (`git stash`): 12 failed
  + 1 error there too. Causes: `httpx2.InvalidURL: Invalid port: ':1]'`
  in client HTTP-transport tests (the sandbox egress-proxy env) and
  `test_permission_error` (tests run as root, so no permission error
  occurs). None of the failures is in the touched files.
- Env: `uv sync --frozen` + `uv run --frozen pytest` per the repo's
  AGENTS.md (uv installed via the official installer; no pip used).

### Docs

No docs page documents the old gate error shape (`docs/migration.md`
is closed to new entries; `docs/servers/handling-errors.md` covers
handler errors, not the lifecycle gate), so no docs change is included
— maintainer to judge.

title: fix(server): flush stdout and ensure line-buffering before restoring fd 1 (#3821)
body:
# PR Draft: Flush stdout and ensure line-buffering before restoring fd 1

**PR Title**: `fix(server): flush stdout and ensure line-buffering before restoring fd 1 (#3821)`
**Branch**: `fix/stdio-flush-line-buffering`

---

## Summary

Resolves #3821: In `stdio_server`, unbuffered writes or missing flush before restoring stdout/fd 1 causes JSON-RPC messages to interleave or hang on client pipes.

### Root Cause
When `stdio_server` starts, fd 1 is diverted to stderr (or `/dev/null`) while the original wire descriptor is maintained privately for JSON-RPC framing. However, when standard streams are connected to pipes, Python's default buffering mode for `sys.stdout` is block-buffered (`line_buffering=False`). Stray writes made to `sys.stdout` (e.g. from sub-libraries or third-party loggers writing without explicit flushes) remain buffered in Python's user-space buffer while fd 1 points to the diversion.

During teardown, `_restore_fd(1, ...)` restores fd 1 back to the wire. If `sys.stdout` is not flushed prior to restoring the descriptor, those buffered stray bytes are flushed *after* fd 1 is restored, dumping arbitrary non-JSON-RPC text directly onto the client transport pipe. This leads to client framing parse errors, corrupted streams, and deadlocks. Additionally, restoring `sys.stdout` without line-buffering leaves subsequent writes prone to blocking or delayed delivery.

### Changes
1. **Flush & Reconfigure on Restore**:
   - In `_restore_fd(fd, private_fd)`: When `fd == 1`, flush `sys.stdout` and call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)` before `os.dup2(private_fd, fd)`.
   - In `_claim_fd(fd, stream, ...)` `release()`: Explicitly flush both `sys.stdout` and `stream`, and reconfigure line buffering before restoration.
2. **Flush on Divert**:
   - In `_claim_fd(...)`: Flush `sys.stdout` and `stream` before redirecting fd 1 to the diversion to ensure pre-existing buffer contents do not spill across fd states.
3. **Line-Buffering on Active Server Stream**:
   - In `stdio_server(...)`: Wrap `stdout_buffer` with `_UnownedTextWrapper(..., line_buffering=True)`.
4. **BlockBuster Test Whitelist**:
   - In `tests/conftest.py`: Allow `os.write`, `io.BufferedWriter.write`, `io.TextIOWrapper.write` in `mcp/server/stdio.py` during `release` and `_restore_fd`.
5. **Regression Test**:
   - Added `test_stdio_server_flushes_stdout_and_ensures_line_buffering_before_restore` in `tests/server/test_stdio.py`, testing unflushed writes during `stdio_server` lifespan are flushed to the diversion, line buffering is ensured on restore, and the client pipe receives zero leaked bytes.

---

title: fix(server): don't log a client session close as an ERROR in the standalone SSE writer
body:
Fixes #3833

## Problem

On the v1.x line, closing a stateful streamable-HTTP session the normal way (the client's
`streamablehttp_client` context exits and sends `DELETE`) logs an `ERROR` with a full traceback:

```
ERROR mcp.server.streamable_http: Error in standalone SSE writer
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ... standalone_sse_writer
    async for event_message in standalone_stream_reader:
anyio.ClosedResourceError
```

`StreamableHTTPServerTransport.terminate()` closes every request stream, including the standalone
GET stream (`GET_STREAM_KEY`), while `standalone_sse_writer` is still iterating it. The resulting
`anyio.ClosedResourceError` is caught by the writer's generic `except Exception: logger.exception(...)`,
so every successfully-closed session leaves an ERROR traceback in the server log and buries real
errors. Nothing actually fails — the calls succeed and the server keeps serving.

## Fix

Catch `anyio.ClosedResourceError` separately in `standalone_sse_writer` and log it at `DEBUG`: a
stream closed under the writer during a client-initiated termination is a normal end of the stream.
All other exceptions keep the existing `logger.exception("Error in standalone SSE writer")`.

## Tests

New in-process regression test in `tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py`:

title: fix(otel): do not mark client span ERROR for JSON-RPC caller-error codes (#3811)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #3811

### Problem
In `JSONRPCDispatcher.send_raw_request()`, every JSON-RPC error response marked the client OTel span `StatusCode.ERROR` with `error.type` set to the error code. Per the OTel GenAI semantic conventions for MCP (`docs/gen-ai/mcp.md`), codes `-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601`, `-32602`, and `-32002` indicate caller-side request errors and should not mark the span `ERROR` (while still recording `rpc.response.status_code`).

### Solution
Always record `rpc.response.status_code = str(outcome.code)`, and only set `error.type` and `StatusCode.ERROR` when `outcome.code` is not in `_CALLER_ERROR_CODES` (`{-32700, -32600, -32601, -32602, -32002}`).

`decode_header_value()` in `src/mcp/shared/inbound.py` documents that a malformed `=?base64?...?=` sentinel yields `None` so callers reject the request with `HEADER_MISMATCH` (HTTP 400). title: fix(stdio): flush sys.stdout before restoring fd 1 in stdio_server (#3821)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #3821

### Problem
While `stdio_server()` is active, `fd 1` is diverted to `stderr` so stray output from tool handlers misses the JSON-RPC wire. However, when `stdout` is a pipe, `sys.stdout` is block-buffered: text written via `print()` inside a tool sits in `sys.stdout`'s buffer and is only flushed at interpreter exit — after `restore_stdout()` has already restored `fd 1` back to the client's JSON-RPC pipe.

### Solution
Flush `sys.stdout` (under `with suppress(OSError, ValueError):`) immediately before calling `restore_stdout()` in the `finally:` block of `stdio_server()`, ensuring any buffered output is written to the diversion (`stderr`) while `fd 1` is still diverted.

title: fix(auth): no error code for a request that presented no credentials
body:
## Summary

`RequireAuthMiddleware` collapses two different failures into one challenge, and never advertises the required scope.

**1. A request that presented no credentials is answered with an error code.** RFC 6750 Section 3.1: a request with no credentials SHOULD NOT include an error code. The gate answered a no-`Authorization` request with `error="invalid_token"` — the same challenge as a token that was presented and rejected.

**2. No challenge ever carried `scope`.** The spec SHOULD include it for both the discovery-time 401 (`#protected-resource-metadata-discovery-requirements`) and the runtime 403 (`#runtime-insufficient-scope-errors`). This SDK's own client reads `scope` out of the header to drive step-up (`utils.py extract_scope_from_www_auth`), so the gap was a resource-server/client asymmetry: the client consumed a parameter the server never sent.

## Changes

`src/mcp/server/auth/middleware/bearer_auth.py`

- `__call__`: the not-authenticated branch now checks whether an `Authorization` header was actually presented. If not, the challenge carries no error code and the body is empty; if a credential was presented and rejected, `error="invalid_token"` is kept. Either way the challenge advertises the required `scope`.
- The 403 branch now passes the required scope so it is named in the challenge.
- `_send_auth_error` takes an optional `scope`, emits it as a `scope="..."` parameter, and allows `error`/`description` to be absent.

The scope string is joined outside the f-string: nested same-type quotes in an f-string need PEP 701 (Python 3.12+), and this project supports 3.11.

## Resulting behaviour

| request | status | `WWW-Authenticate` | body |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `Authorization` | 401 | `resource_metadata`, `scope` | empty |
| invalid token | 401 | `error="invalid_token"`, `resource_metadata`, `scope` | `{"error": ..., "error_description": ...}` |
| insufficient scope | 403 | `error="insufficient_scope"`, `scope`, `resource_metadata` | `{"error": ..., "error_description": ...}` |

## Tests

`tests/interaction/auth/test_bearer.py` and `tests/docs_src/test_authorization.py` updated to pin the corrected challenge (the previous ones pinned the old one via `inline_snapshot`). `tests/interaction/_requirements.py` drops the now-resolved `divergence` records on `hosting:auth:missing-401`, `hosting:auth:scope-403` and `hosting:auth:invalid-401`.

`docs/run/authorization.md` updated so the tutorial shows the two cases separately.

Local run: 276 passed, 1 xfailed (`tests/interaction/auth/`, `tests/interaction/test_coverage.py`, `tests/client/test_auth.py`, `tests/docs_src/test_authorization.py`); `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

## Note for the reviewer

The maintainer comment on the issue suggests the backend should signal "no credentials" distinctly (e.g. a sentinel/exception) rather than the header check used here. The header check gets the same split with a smaller diff, but I am happy to switch to backend signalling if that is preferred. The `scope` value is the scopes required for the current request — `self.required_scopes` when the middleware is instantiated per route — not `settings.required_scopes` blindly.

Closes #3769

title: fix(client): end the read stream when stdout hits EOF on a live server
body:
Fixes #3804

<!-- Provide a brief summary of your changes -->
When a stdio server closes stdout but keeps running, `stdio_client` now ends the session instead of hanging. `stdout_reader` terminates the process before draining its remaining output when the reader is finishing for any reason other than shutdown.

## Motivation and Context

`stdout_reader` closes the read stream from inside `async with read_stream_writer:`, but its `finally` block runs `_drain_stdout` first. That drain is a shielded `while True: await process.stdout.receive()`. If the server closed stdout without exiting, the drain waits on pipes that stay open as long as the process lives and that nobody will write to again. The writer is never closed, so the session never sees the end of the read stream, and any request waiting on the dispatcher waits until the caller's own timeout, or forever.

A crashed logging wrapper or a closed fd is enough to get there; nothing about it is unusual for a caller.

Terminating before the drain fixes it: the process goes, its pipes close, the drain sees EOF, the writer closes, and pending and later requests fail with `CONNECTION_CLOSED`. Shutdown is excluded, because it runs its own stop sequence in `_stop_server_process` and the `shutting_down` flag now has to be visible inside the reader task (an `anyio.Event` replaces the `bool`).

The drain keeps its purpose: a server flushing its last output must not block on a full pipe. It just runs against a process that is closing its pipes.

This also makes the read side symmetric with `stdin_writer`, which already closes the read stream when a write fails, with the comment "so the server sees the connection end instead of a request hanging forever".

## How Has This Been Tested?

Tested with the in-process `FakeProcess` used by the rest of `tests/client/test_stdio.py`, plus the reproducer from the issue against real subprocesses.

- New test `test_stdout_eof_while_the_server_keeps_running_ends_the_read_stream`: EOF on stdout closes the read stream and terminates the still-running server.
- Existing `test_a_failed_write_to_a_live_server_closes_the_read_stream_instead_of_hanging` asserted `terminated == []` for the same shape (a live server outliving the session). It now asserts the server was terminated, which is the behaviour the fix introduces; its other two assertions (read stream ends, output still drained) are unchanged.
- `pytest tests/client tests/shared` on `af4c6f4`: `1793 passed, 5 failed` before, `1794 passed, 5 failed` after. The 5 failures are `blockbuster` complaining about `os.stat` in streamable-http tests and fail identically without this change.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

With the issue's reproducer and a real server that closes stdout after `initialize` and sleeps: `list_tools()` hangs until the caller's timeout before, and raises `MCPError(-32000, 'Connection closed')` immediately after.

## Breaking Changes

No API change. A server that closes stdout and keeps running is now ended rather than left attached to a session that can no longer receive anything.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

On the second comment in the issue: the reproducer no longer hangs on `main` either, which is why I tested against the internal state rather than the caller-visible symptom. What `main` avoids is the pending request, because the drain's `while True` is left when the process eventually exits. title: shared: treat a non-ASCII base64 header value as malformed
body:
Fixes #3817

`decode_header_value` promised in its docstring that a malformed sentinel yields `None`, but it only caught `binascii.Error`. `base64.b64decode` raises a plain `ValueError` when the payload has non-ASCII characters in it, so a raw `Mcp-Name: =?base64?\xe9?=` slipped past the decoder, out of `classify_inbound_request`, and out of `handle_modern_request` as an unhandled exception — HTTP 500 instead of a rejection.

## Motivation and Context

Every other undecodable sentinel already produces `HEADER_MISMATCH` / 400 (`=?base64?!!!?=`, `=?base64?gA==?=`, bad UTF-8). The non-ASCII case is the only one that escalates into a server error, and it's the one a fuzzer finds first — which is how it was reported. `Mcp-Param-*` values go through the same helper, so they were affected too.

Fix is one `except` clause. `binascii.Error` is a subclass of `ValueError`, so catching `(binascii.Error, ValueError)` keeps the existing bad-alphabet / bad-padding behaviour identical and adds the non-ASCII case.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Reproduced first with the ASGI script from the issue on `af4c6f4` (2.3.0):

```
b'echo'                 200
b'=?base64?ZWNobw==?='  200
b'=?base64?!!!?='       400 HEADER_MISMATCH
b'=?base64?\xe9?='      500 Internal Server Error   <- before the fix
```

After the change the high-byte header answers `400` with `-32020`, same as the other malformed sentinels.

Two tests added:

- `tests/shared/test_inbound.py` — new case in the existing `test_decode_header_value_returns_none_for_malformed_sentinel` parametrization for `=?base64?\xe9?=`.
- `tests/server/test_streamable_http_modern.py::test_handle_modern_request_rejects_non_ascii_base64_name_header_with_400` — end-to-end over the ASGI transport, asserts 400 + `HEADER_MISMATCH`.

Fixes #3712

## Motivation and Context

`_create_output_model` (in `func_metadata.py`) resolves an ordinary class's
field hints with `get_type_hints(type_annotation)`, which strips `Annotated`
metadata. As a result a field declared `Annotated[int, Field(gt=0)]` collapses
to a bare `int` when the return annotation is turned into a structured-output
model:

- the generated output schema loses `exclusiveMinimum: 0` (only `type: integer` remains), and
- `convert_result(...)` accepts an out-of-bound value such as `0` and returns `structured_content={"value": 0}` instead of raising `ValidationError`.

Pydantic itself rejects `0` for the exact same annotation, and the equivalent
`BaseModel`/`TypedDict` paths preserve the constraint, so the behaviour is
inconsistent and a declared bound is silently discarded.

The fix passes `include_extras=True` so the `Annotated` metadata survives into
the synthesized Pydantic model — the same way the TypedDict path already
resolves its hints (`get_type_hints(td_type, include_extras=True)`).

Added `test_structured_output_ordinary_class_keeps_annotated_field_constraints`,
which asserts the constraint appears in the schema (`exclusiveMinimum: 0`),

title: fix(shared): stop concurrent int/string request ids from colliding in _in_flight
body:
# fix(shared): stop concurrent int/string request ids from colliding in _in_flight

Fixes #3807

## Summary

- `JSONRPCDispatcher._in_flight` keyed inbound requests by
  `coerce_request_id(req.id)`, which folds `"7"` and `7` into one dict slot.
  Two concurrent requests whose ids differ only in JSON-RPC type
  blind-overwrote each other, and a `notifications/cancelled` naming one
  cancelled whichever was stored — the other ran to completion and could no
  longer be cancelled.
- Store in-flight requests under the **verbatim** id so distinct wire
  representations stay distinct. Cancellation looks up the exact id first
  and falls back to coerced/stringified forms so a peer that echoes a
  different type between request and cancel still cancels the request
  (the existing `test_cancelled_correlates_across_string_and_int_request_id_forms`
  passes unchanged in both parametrizations).

## Reproduction

Unmodified SDK, stdio, two concurrent requests with ids `"9007199254740991"`
(string) and `9007199254740991` (int), plus a `notifications/cancelled` for
the string id (see the reproduction script linked in #3807):

- on `main`: the cancel hits the **int-id** request (they share the coerced
  slot); the string-id request answers, the int-id request never does.
- after the fix: the cancel hits only the string-id request; the int-id
  request answers normally.

## Fix

`src/mcp/shared/jsonrpc_dispatcher.py` — three hunks:

1. **Store** (`_dispatch_request`): `self._in_flight[req.id] = ...` —
   verbatim id, no coercion.
2. **Cancel** (`_dispatch_notification`): exact-id lookup first; if missed,
   try the coerced id and its stringified form so cross-type echo still
   correlates.
3. **Delete** (`_handle_request`): pop by verbatim id, matching the store.

The `pending` (outbound correlation) table is untouched: its coercion is
correct and needed for response matching.

## Validation

New regression test `test_peer_cancel_does_not_cross_request_id_types`:

| case | on `main` (af4c6f4) | after |
|---|---|---|
| concurrent `"9007199254740991"` and `9007199254740991`, cancel the string one | int-id request cancelled (wrong); string-id answered | string-id cancelled; int-id answers |
| cross-type echo: cancel with int for a string-id request | passes | passes (coerced fallback) |
| cross-type echo: cancel with string for an int-id request | passes | passes (stringified fallback) |

The regression test fails on unmodified `main` (the int-id request gets no
response) and passes after. Full `tests/shared/test_jsonrpc_dispatcher.py`:
**80 passed, 0 failed** — zero regressions, including both parametrizations
of the cross-type correlation test.

## Scope

- 2 files: `src/mcp/shared/jsonrpc_dispatcher.py` and
  `tests/shared/test_jsonrpc_dispatcher.py`.
- No change to the outbound `pending` table, `_allocate_id`, the direct
  dispatcher's collision detection, or any handler/cancellation semantics
  beyond the id-keying described above.

title: fix(mcpserver): honor warn_on_duplicate_resources for URI templates
body:
Fixes #3813.

`ResourceManager.add_template()` registers templates with a bare dict assignment, so a second `@server.resource("file://doc/{id}")` silently replaces the first handler. `add_resource()`, `PromptManager.add_prompt()` and the documented `warn_on_duplicate_resources` setting all do the opposite: warn (when enabled) and keep the handler that was registered first.

That divergence is reachable without any unusual setup — two modules or extensions that both declare the same URI template end up with whichever one was imported last, and nothing in the logs says so:

```python
server = MCPServer(warn_on_duplicate_resources=True)

@server.resource("file://doc")
def doc1() -> str: return "v1"

@server.resource("file://doc")
def doc2() -> str: return "v2"

@server.resource("file://doc/{id}")
def template1(id: str) -> str: return "template_v1"

@server.resource("file://doc/{id}")
def template2(id: str) -> str: return "template_v2"
```

Before: the static resource warns and keeps `doc1`, the template is replaced by `template2` with no warning. After: both warn and keep the first registration, and `add_template()` returns the template that is actually registered (matching `add_resource()`'s return contract, now documented in the docstring).

Tests added to `tests/server/mcpserver/resources/test_resource_manager.py`, mirroring the existing resource-duplicate tests:

- `test_add_duplicate_template` — the second registration returns the first template, `list_templates()` has one entry, and the retained handler is the first one.
- `test_warn_on_duplicate_templates` — logs `Resource template already exists: ...`.
- `test_disable_warn_on_duplicate_templates` — silent when `warn_on_duplicate_resources=False`.

Results: on `main` the first two fail (`2 failed, 12 passed`); with the change the file is `14 passed`. `ruff format` / `ruff check`: clean.

One judgement call worth flagging: I kept the existing template rather than replacing it, because that is what the sibling registration paths do and what the flag's docstring describes. If you would rather have last-registration-wins with a warning, the change is a one-line flip and I will adjust.

title: Keep unknown keys on client and server capabilities
body:
Fixes #3640

`ClientCapabilities` and `ServerCapabilities` are documented as "not a closed set", and the schema doesn't forbid extra keys, but both the public models and the generated wire models dropped them. A server couldn't advertise a top-level capability like `events` (ChatGPT's MCP Events) without patching the serialized result in middleware.

Both capability models now use `extra="allow"`, in the public types and in the wire models (via `OPEN_CLASSES` in `scripts/gen_surface_types.py`). Nested known capability objects stay closed.

## AI Disclaimer

This PR was developed with the assistance of either Claude or Codex. I've reviewed and verified the changes.

title: fix(snippets): encode thumbnail as PNG in images example (#3805)
body:
Fixes #3805

In `examples/snippets/servers/images.py`, the `create_thumbnail` tool previously returned `Image(data=img.tobytes(), format="png")`. Pillow's `tobytes()` produces raw uncompressed RGB pixel bytes lacking PNG file headers, chunks, and compression, causing downstream clients that attempt to decode the data URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`) to fail with `UnidentifiedImageError` or invalid image decode errors.

This PR encodes the resized image into a valid in-memory PNG stream via `io.BytesIO()` and `img.save(buffer, format="PNG")`, returning true PNG bytes. An integration test has also been added in `tests/server/mcpserver/test_integration.py` to verify valid PNG container headers and correct thumbnail dimensions.

## Motivation and Context
Fixes #3805. Clients calling `create_thumbnail` expect valid PNG encoded bytes as indicated by `format="png"`.

title: Relay stdio stderr for Jupyter and other non-file errlogs
body:
Fixes #156

`stdio_client` keeps handing a real file to the child, and pipes stderr into `errlog.write()` for every other text stream. Jupyter, `io.StringIO`, pytest's capsys, and logging shims no longer lose server stderr or fail the spawn.

## Motivation and Context

`stdio_client` passed `errlog` straight to `anyio.open_process(stderr=...)`. That only works when the child can inherit a descriptor that is the stream you are reading.

Two failures hide a server that crashes on startup:

- Jupyter / ipykernel: `sys.stderr` is an `OutStream` (`io.TextIOBase`, not a `TextIOWrapper`). `fileno()` returns a copy of the kernel's original fd 2, so the child writes to the terminal the notebook was launched from and the cell stays empty.
- No descriptor: `io.StringIO`, pytest's capsys, and logging shims that only implement `write()`. `fileno()` raises, and on Windows the spawn itself fails.

Detecting Jupyter by name is not enough. A working `fileno()` can still point past the notebook.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Dual mode:

- A `TextIOWrapper` with a working `fileno()` is still inherited. The server reports fd 2's identity, which matches the file.
- Anything else text-like is spawned with `stderr=PIPE`. An async reader copies decoded chunks into `errlog.write()` (`errors="replace"`).
- Shutdown waits up to 0.5s for that reader to see EOF before closing the pipe, so lines written while the server exits are not dropped. A descendant that keeps the pipe open does not hang shutdown.
- A closed or rejecting `errlog` (including a broken `sys.stderr`) loses only the failed write. The reader keeps draining so the child cannot block on a full pipe.
- `None` (pythonw) and `subprocess.DEVNULL` still go to the spawn unchanged. A binary buffer is still rejected at spawn.

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/client/test_stdio.py tests/transports/stdio/test_lifecycle.py tests/transports/stdio/test_posix.py tests/interaction/transports/test_stdio.py -q
```

60 passed. `src/mcp/client/stdio.py` is at 100% statement and branch coverage on that run. `uv run --frozen pyright` reported 0 errors. Ruff check on the touched files was clean.

## Breaking Changes

None for callers who pass a real file or the default terminal `sys.stderr`. Streams that are not files now receive stderr through `write()` instead of failing or inheriting an unrelated descriptor.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist

- [ ] I am assigned to the linked issue (or it is labeled `help wanted`, or I'm a maintainer)
- [x] I have disclosed any AI assistance and can explain the change in my own words
- [x] I have read the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Additional context

Evan approved opening this PR for #156.

AI assistance was used to implement and test the change. The behavior is covered by real-subprocess tests (file identity, `StringIO` including the line written while exiting, and a notebook-style stream whose `fileno()` points at another file) and by in-process tests for capsys, a write-only logging shim, a closed `errlog`, cancellation during shutdown, and undecodable bytes.

On the Windows selector-loop fallback, `FallbackProcess` now wraps a stderr pipe the same way it already wraps stdout. Those tests are skipped on Linux, where the shared relay was run.

title: [v1.x] Fix refreshed access tokens not reaching tool handlers
body:
Fixes #1250

**The bug.** On the v1 line, a client that refreshes its access token mid-session keeps sending the new token and the token verifier accepts it, but tools calling `get_access_token()` still receive the token the session was opened with. I reproduced it on this branch (Streamable HTTP with a plain `TokenVerifier`): initialize and call a tool presenting token A, then present token B in the same session - the tool still sees A. For what it's worth, the same scenario already works on `main` (v2), where the dispatcher propagates each message's sender context into the handler; this PR is for v1.x, which is what the reports in #1250 are running (1.16 / 1.19).

**Root cause.** `AuthContextMiddleware` sets `auth_context_var` on each HTTP request's task, but handlers run in the session's long-lived task, whose context still holds the session-opening request's user. The per-request data needed is already being carried: both HTTP transports attach the current Starlette request to the message metadata, and its scope holds the user authenticated for that request.

**The change** (+17 lines in `src/mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py`). In `_handle_request` - the same place that already re-applies the per-request `request_ctx` from the message metadata - apply `auth_context_var` from the attached request's scope for the duration of the handler, and reset it in the `finally` next to the `request_ctx` reset. No public API changes. Transports that attach no request (stdio) are untouched, and because the value is applied per request at dispatch, parallel sessions cannot observe each other's tokens. This is the layer #1998 aimed at (thanks @bgaidioz, the repro repo helped pin this down); that draft has been sitting untouched since February and predates the current shape of this function, so this is a fresh version of it with fuller tests.

**Tests.**
- `tests/issues/test_1250_refreshed_access_token.py` - end-to-end over Streamable HTTP, in process: a refreshed token is what the tool sees in the same session, and two parallel sessions, held in flight at the same time on a barrier so they genuinely overlap, each see only their own current token.
- `tests/server/lowlevel/test_auth_context_from_request.py` - dispatch level: the scope user is applied for the handler and reset afterwards; no user in scope, a non-`AuthenticatedUser` scope user, an attached object without a scope, and no metadata at all each leave the context empty.
- Without the fix, 3 of these fail (both end-to-end tests and the scope-user unit test); with it, all pass, and every line/branch added in `server.py` is covered. Locally `tests/server/auth`, `tests/server/lowlevel`, `tests/server/fastmcp` (318 tests) and `tests/issues` pass; the handful of failures/errors in the socket-based transport tests reproduce identically on the pristine branch in my sandbox, so they look environmental rather than related. `ruff format`/`ruff check` are clean and `pyright` reports no errors on the changed file.

## Summary

`ClientSessionGroup` currently fetches only the first page of each server’s tools, resources, and prompts. Later-page components are silently omitted, leaving valid tools unavailable through `group.call_tool()`.

title: fix(client): avoid stack growth during SSE reconnection
body:
Fixes #3791

## Summary

Long-lived requests can fail after repeated productive SSE reconnects because `_handle_reconnection()` recursively awaits itself, accumulating Python stack frames.

In a deterministic reproduction, each connection delivers a notification with a new event ID before closing. At the default recursion limit, the client fails after approximately 970 connections with `CONNECTION_CLOSED` and “reconnection attempts were exhausted,” before the final response arrives. Raising the recursion limit allows the same scenario to complete all 1,500 connections.

Replace recursive reconnection with an iterative loop so productive resumptions can continue without accumulating stack frames.

## Changes

- Replace recursive calls with a loop carrying the current event ID, retry delay, and attempt count.
- Exit each response context before opening the next connection.
- Preserve existing retry accounting, resumption-token callbacks, cancellation, and terminal error handling.
- Add a regression covering 1,500 connections, ordered delivery of 1,499 notifications, resumption cursors, and the final response without modifying Python’s recursion limit.

This addresses stack growth separately from the no-progress retry-budget behavior tracked in #2393 and proposed in #2395.

## Validation

- Confirmed the new regression fails on unmodified code and passes with this change.
- **macOS / Python 3.13:** all 120 transport tests passed.
- **Linux / Python 3.12:** full suite passed—6,227 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- Coverage: **100%**, with `strict-no-cover` passing.
- Ruff lint, formatting, Pyright, and `git diff --check` passed.

The reproduction uses a synthetic HTTP peer; this failure has not been verified in a production deployment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation. I reproduced the failure and ran the transport tests, lint, formatting, and type checks locally.

title: fix(mcpserver): bind positional-only handler parameters in tools, prompts, resources (#3760)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #3760

### Problem
In `modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk`, handler execution uniformly unpacked arguments as keyword arguments only (`**kwargs`):
- `FuncMetadata.call_fn` (`src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py`)
- `Prompt.render` (`src/mcp/server/mcpserver/prompts/base.py`)
- `ResourceTemplate.create_resource` (`src/mcp/server/mcpserver/resources/templates.py`)
- `_resolve` (`src/mcp/server/mcpserver/resolve.py`)

When handlers use positional-only arguments (`def handler(x: str, /)` or C-extension callables), invocation fails at runtime with:
`TypeError: handler() got some positional-only arguments passed as keyword arguments: 'x'`
or Pydantic `ValidationError: Missing required positional only argument`.

### Solution (Minimal & Dependency-Free)
1. Added `split_positional_args(fn, kwargs)` helper to `src/mcp/shared/_callable_inspection.py`:
   - Inspects `inspect.signature(fn)` for `inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY`.
   - Returns ordered `(tuple(pos_args), remaining_kwargs)`, preserving default values when optional parameters are not provided in `kwargs`.
   - Uses only Python standard library (`inspect`).
2. Integrated `split_positional_args` into the 4 handler invocation points so positional-only parameters are passed as `*pos_args` while remaining arguments are passed as `**kwargs`.
3. Added test coverage in `tests/server/mcpserver/test_posonly_handlers.py` verifying tool, prompt, and resource template execution with positional-only arguments.

title: fix(client): keep a session's exit stack when a server has no components
body:
`_aggregate_components` treated an empty prompt/resource/tool sweep as "the server gave us nothing" and deleted the session's exit stack.

On the `connect_with_session` path no stack is ever registered, so the `del` raised a bare `KeyError` and the connection failed outright. On the `connect_to_server` path the stack was removed without being closed, so `disconnect_from_server` had nothing left to tear down and the transport stayed open until the whole group exited.

The premise was wrong in the first place: the group never calls `list_resource_templates`, so a server whose entire surface is a resource template also looks componentless to aggregation.

Fixes #3384

title: [v1.x] Resolve a failed SSE message POST instead of hanging the caller
body:
Fixes #2110 (the SSE part, on v1.x; #3278 covers main)

Backports the SSE half of #3278 to v1.x: a failed message POST now resolves its request with a JSON-RPC error instead of leaving the caller hanging.

## Motivation and Context

`sse_client`'s `post_writer` called `raise_for_status()` on every message POST and swallowed the error in a catch-all. A request whose POST failed (a 429 from a rate limiter, a 401, a refused connection) was never resolved: its caller waited for its own timeout, or forever without one. The write loop died with it, so every later message was dropped. We hit this in production: a 429 from a rate limiter in front of an MCP server left an agent's tool call waiting 90 minutes for an unrelated outer timeout.

## How Has This Been Tested?

10 new tests in `tests/shared/test_sse.py`, all of which fail on unpatched v1.x (7 hang, 3 end with a closed stream or the wrong error):

- non-2xx answers (302, 401, 429, 500) and a refused connection reach the caller, and the session keeps working;
- a 404 maps to "Session terminated" only while the endpoint carries a session id;
- a failed notification is only logged;
- a server request answered while a request's POST is failing (the test times out if the error is delivered inline);
- a failure whose error can no longer be delivered, after the SSE stream ended, is contained.

The full suite passes with 100% coverage, along with pyright and ruff. The SSE tests also pass on 3.10 with lowest-direct deps and on 3.14.

## Breaking Changes

None. A caller that used to hang now gets an `McpError`, and later messages keep flowing.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist

- [ ] I am assigned to the linked issue (or it is labeled `help wanted`, or I'm a maintainer): asked on #2110
- [x] I have disclosed any AI assistance and can explain the change in my own words
- [x] I have read the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Additional context

The outcomes match #3278 on main: a non-2xx status gives `INTERNAL_ERROR` "Server returned an error response", or `INVALID_REQUEST` "Session terminated" for a 404 while the endpoint carries a session id; an error before any response gives `CONNECTION_CLOSED` "Failed to send message: …".

One v1.x-specific difference: the error is delivered from a task of its own. v1.x `ClientSession` answers server requests inline in its receive loop, so a reply can be waiting on the write stream just as the error needs the receive loop, and delivering it from the write loop deadlocks.

title: Separate advertised scopes_supported from required_scopes
body:
Fixes #3778

`AuthSettings.required_scopes` is used both to refuse tokens (`RequireAuthMiddleware`) and as the Protected Resource Metadata's `scopes_supported`, so a server cannot advertise a scope that only some handlers check — a write scope, for example — without challenging for it on every request. Clients that take their scope request from `scopes_supported` then never ask for the write scope.

## Change

- `AuthSettings.scopes_supported: list[str] | None` (new, optional): the scopes advertised in the Protected Resource Metadata.
- Both protected-resource route builders (`mcpserver` and `lowlevel`) use `auth.scopes_supported or auth.required_scopes`, so existing servers are unchanged and the challenge still uses `required_scopes` only.

## Tests

`tests/server/auth/test_protected_resource.py`:

- `test_scopes_supported_advertised_separately_from_required_scopes`: an `MCPServer` with `required_scopes=["returns:read"]` and `scopes_supported=["returns:read", "returns:write"]` serves `scopes_supported` as both scopes over `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- `test_scopes_supported_defaults_to_required_scopes`: without the new field, the metadata still advertises `required_scopes`.

Verified: `pytest tests/server/auth/test_protected_resource.py -q` -> **16 passed**; with only the three source files reverted, the advertising test fails (the field is ignored and the metadata lists only `returns:read`). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on all four files.

Note: the issue author offered to open this PR; this is unassigned work on the same proposal, and the tests above are new. Happy to adjust the field name or the default if you prefer a different shape.

On connections that negotiate `2025-11-25` or earlier, `serialize_server_result("initialize", ...)` sieves the result through the 2025 wire model, which has no `extensions` field, so a server could never advertise an extension (e.g. MCP Apps) to a legacy client.

title: fix(client): reject userinfo, dot segments and fragments in CIMD client_id URLs
body:
Fixes #3768

> Scope note: this PR covers item 2 of the issue (CIMD `client_id` URL validation). Item 1, issuer string normalisation, is a behaviour change on the validation path and I'd rather land it separately if maintainers want it.

### 🔗 Related issues

- #3768 (item 2)

### 📋 What's the problem?

`is_valid_client_metadata_url()` enforced only two of the rules that draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document section 3 puts on a client metadata document URL: `https` and a non-root path. On `main` today:

```python
>>> from mcp.client.auth.utils import is_valid_client_metadata_url as v
>>> v("https://user:secret@example.com/client")
True
>>> v("https://example.com/path/../client")
True
>>> v("https://example.com/client#section")
True
```

The authorization server is still the binding check, so this is not a security hole by itself — but the client's pre-flight check accepts URLs it already knows are unusable, and the failure only shows up later in the auth flow.

### 🛠️ The fix

`is_valid_client_metadata_url()` now also rejects:

- URLs with `parsed.username` or `parsed.password`
- paths containing a `.` or `..` segment (percent-decoded first — RFC 3986 normalises `%2E` to `.` for dot-segment removal, so `/%2E%2E/client` is a `..` segment)
- URLs with a non-empty fragment

Query strings, ports and dots inside a segment (`/path.with.dots/client`) stay valid; the draft does not forbid them.

### 🧪 Testing

```
$ uv run --frozen pytest tests/client/test_auth.py -q -k "is_valid_client_metadata_url"
19 passed
```

Seven rows of the parametrised test are new and fail on `main`:

```
$ git checkout main -- src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py
$ uv run --frozen pytest tests/client/test_auth.py -q -k "is_valid_client_metadata_url"
7 failed, 12 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both touched files.

title: fix(mcpserver): handle bare typing.Dict and typing sequence generics in func_metadata
body:
Fixes #3771

## Motivation and Context
In `src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py`, return type inspection behaved inconsistently for unsubscripted `typing` generic counterparts compared to standard built-in types:
1. `typing.Dict`: `get_origin(typing.Dict)` is `dict` but `get_args(typing.Dict)` is `()`. It fell through the `len(args) == 2` check into the `else` branch, mistakenly forcing `wrap_output = True` (wrapped in `{"result": ...}`) instead of being treated as a top-level JSON object like `dict` or `dict[str, Any]`.
2. `typing.List` / `typing.Tuple`: `typing.List in (list, tuple)` evaluates to `False`, bypassing the opt-out gate at line 449 and unintentionally producing a wrapped Pydantic output model.

title: fix(auth): parse fractional expires_in and stop treating expiry 0 as no expiry
body:
## Scope correction (this PR stays closed)

I opened this as two defects with user-visible impact and I was wrong about the impact. Checking the path end to end after the fact:

- `OAuthToken.expires_in` is `int | None`, and pydantic rejects both `"3599.5"` and `3599.5` with a `ValidationError` before `calculate_token_expiry` is ever called. `float()` there therefore does not repair any reachable flow; it only makes a defensive helper match its own annotation and docstring.
- `token_expiry_time` is written only from `calculate_token_expiry` (or `None`), so a literal `0.0` is not reachable through SDK code. The falsy-zero change is hardening for state a caller supplies, not a bug fix.

The expiry boundary is the real defect in this area and a maintainer already has it: #3761.

So this is a two-line hardening patch on defensive paths, not a bug fix, and the repository's contribution policy is clear that a change still has to justify the contract it adds. Leaving it closed unless a maintainer wants the hardening. The evidence for the claim above, measured on current `main`:

```
OAuthToken(access_token='a', expires_in='3599.5')  -> ValidationError (expires_in)
OAuthToken(access_token='a', expires_in=3599.5)    -> ValidationError (expires_in)
calculate_token_expiry('3599.5')                   -> ValueError: invalid literal for int()
```

## What the diff does, described accurately

`src/mcp/shared/auth_utils.py`: `calculate_token_expiry` declares `int | str | None` and documents string handling, but calls `int(expires_in)`, which raises on a fractional string and truncates a float. Using `float()` makes the helper agree with its own annotation. No reachable caller benefits today.

`src/mcp/client/auth/oauth2.py`: `is_token_valid()` reads `not self.token_expiry_time`, which conflates `None` ("no expiry declared") with any falsy value, including `0.0`. Comparing against `None` explicitly states the intended meaning. No SDK path currently produces `0.0`.

`tests/shared/test_auth_utils.py` and `tests/client/test_auth.py` carry the matching tests for both, including the `None`, integer, numeric-string, fractional-string and float inputs the annotation already claimed to support.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/client tests/shared -q
1804 passed, 1 xfailed

uv run ruff check src/mcp/shared/auth_utils.py src/mcp/client/auth/oauth2.py \
  tests/shared/test_auth_utils.py tests/client/test_auth.py
All checks passed!
```

title: fix(auth): return RFC 6749 compliant OAuth error codes for token and revoke (#3723)
body:
## Description
Addresses #3723 by ensuring RFC 6749 §5.2 and RFC 7009 §2.2.1 compliance for OAuth 2.0 error responses in the token and revocation endpoints:

1. **Token endpoint (`/token`)**:
   - When a requested grant type is unsupported by the authorization server (e.g. `client_credentials`, `password`), return `unsupported_grant_type` (status 400) rather than failing discriminator validation with `invalid_request`.
   - When an authenticated client is not authorized to use the requested grant type (i.e. `token_request.grant_type not in client_info.grant_types`), return `unauthorized_client` (status 400) per RFC 6749 §5.2 ("The authenticated client is not authorized to use this authorization grant type"), rather than `unsupported_grant_type`.
2. **Revocation endpoint (`/revoke`)**:
   - When client authentication fails (`AuthenticationError`), return `error="invalid_client"` with status 401 per RFC 7009 §2.2.1 and RFC 6749 §5.2 ("Client authentication failed"), rather than `unauthorized_client`.
   - Extended `RevocationErrorResponse` to allow `invalid_client`.

## Testing
- Added regression tests in `tests/server/auth/test_error_handling.py`:
  - `test_token_unsupported_grant_type_returns_unsupported_grant_type`
  - `test_token_unauthorized_client_grant_type_returns_unauthorized_client`
  - `test_revoke_invalid_client_authentication_returns_401`
- Updated `test_identity_assertion.py` to assert `unauthorized_client` when a registered client is not authorized for the grant.
- Verified all 175 tests in `tests/server/auth` and `tests/interaction/auth` pass.
- Formatted and linted with `ruff`.

Closes #3723

title: Give bare `dict`, `set` and `frozenset` return annotations structured output
body:
Fixes #3725

A bare `-> dict` now gets the same structured output as `-> dict[str, Any]`, and a bare `-> set` / `-> frozenset` is wrapped in `{"result": ...}` like their parameterized forms. A bare `-> list` / `-> tuple` deliberately stays unstructured, and `structured_output=True` now wraps it instead of raising.

## Motivation and Context

Bare builtins fell through to the "other class" branch of `_create_output_model`, where `get_type_hints(dict)` is `{}`, so the tool silently got no `outputSchema` and no `structuredContent`. With `structured_output=True` it raised `return type <class 'dict'> is not serializable`, which reads as if a dict weren't serializable.

| Annotation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `-> dict` | no schema | `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}`, unwrapped |
| `-> set`, `-> frozenset` | no schema | wrapped, `{"type": "array", "uniqueItems": true, "items": {}}` |
| `-> list`, `-> tuple` | no schema | no schema (on purpose); wrapped with `structured_output=True` |

### Why bare `list` / `tuple` stay unstructured

`_convert_to_content` renders content blocks found in a list or tuple as blocks, and `_returns_content` already opts `list[ImageContent]` and friends out of structured output so the image isn't also echoed into `structuredContent`. A bare `list` says nothing about its items, so it may hold blocks too: a `-> list` tool returning `[Image(...), {...}]` would send the image twice, once as a block and once as base64 in `structuredContent`. Some clients then render the JSON instead of the picture, others put the base64 in the model's context. `set` / `frozenset` can't hold content blocks (they aren't hashable), so wrapping them is safe.

FastMCP made the same call (`function_parsing.py`: bare `list`/`tuple` produce no output schema for this reason, while bare `dict` and `set` get one). `list[X]` and `structured_output=True` remain the explicit opt-ins.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Bare `list` / `tuple` added to `test_content_block_return_annotation_yields_no_output_schema`.
- `test_structured_output_true_wraps_a_bare_list`, `test_a_bare_list_inside_a_union_keeps_its_schema`, `test_a_bare_dict_is_structured_like_dict_str_any` and `test_a_bare_set_is_wrapped` snapshot both `output_schema` and the full `CallToolResult`.
- Full suite passes; coverage 100%, `strict-no-cover`, ruff and pyright clean.

## Breaking Changes

Tools annotated with a bare `dict`, `set` or `frozenset` start publishing an `outputSchema` and validating their result against it, exactly as `dict[str, Any]` / `set[Any]` do today. Values that used to be dumped as text with `to_json(..., fallback=str)` and now fail as a tool error (`is_error=True`):

- a bare-`dict` tool returning non-`str` keys, e.g. `{1: "a"}`;
- a `None` return from a `-> dict` / `-> set` tool;
- a value pydantic can't serialize to JSON, e.g. an instance of an arbitrary class inside the dict or set.

Bare `list` / `tuple` tools are unchanged unless they pass `structured_output=True`, which used to raise. Only a bare `list` / `tuple` as the whole annotation is opted out; nested ones (`list | None`, `dict | list`, `list[list]`) keep the wrapped schema they publish today.

title: Drop generated titles from tool input and output schemas
body:
`MCPServer` tools no longer publish the titles pydantic and the SDK generate in `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`. Titles set explicitly with `Field(title=...)` are kept.

## Motivation and Context

Every tool schema carried titles that only repeat information already there:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {"title": "Query", "type": "string"},
    "limit": {"default": 10, "title": "Limit", "type": "integer"}
  },
  "required": ["query"],
  "title": "search_booksArguments"
}
```

`inputSchema` is what clients hand to the model, so these are tokens on every tool, every turn, with no information. Now:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {"type": "string"},
    "limit": {"default": 10, "type": "integer"}
  },
  "required": ["query"]
}
```

What is dropped:

- Field titles pydantic derives from the property name (`"Query"`, `"Result"`), via `GenerateJsonSchema.field_title_should_be_set`. This only governs the derived title, so an explicit `Field(title=...)` still lands in the schema.
- The `<func>Arguments` root title of `inputSchema`, the `<func>Output` root title of a wrapped `{"result": ...}` output, and the `<func>DictOutput` title of `dict[str, X]` outputs. These name models the SDK creates internally; the `DictOutput` one only existed to keep the schema identical when its `RootModel` was removed in #3470.
- The parameter-name title given to unannotated parameters.

What is kept: explicit `Field(title=...)` titles, and the class-name titles of user types (`"title": "Book"` for a `-> Book` tool, and in `$defs`).

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Updated the schema expectations across the suite (inline snapshots regenerated with `--inline-snapshot=fix`, literal dicts edited by hand).
- Added `test_tool_schemas_keep_only_titles_set_explicitly`, which checks that explicit titles survive on both the input and output side.
- Full suite passes; coverage 100%, `strict-no-cover` and pyright clean.

## Breaking Changes

No code changes needed, but `tools/list` output changes: the titles above disappear from `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`. Validation is unaffected, since `title` is an annotation keyword. A client that displayed or keyed on those generated titles would see them gone.

title: security: tool description pinning, injection scan, DNS rebinding default fix
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes three security issues identified during a full static audit of the Python SDK (128 files, ruff + pyright clean, 244 tests pass):

- **Rug-pull attack (CWE-345):** `_absorb_tool_listing()` accepted re-fetched tool descriptions after a `tools/list_changed` notification with no integrity check. A malicious server can serve clean descriptions for N interactions, then send the notification and return poisoned descriptions on re-fetch. Fix: SHA-256 pin each description on first sight; any subsequent change drops the updated version and logs a security warning. Runs for all protocol versions (not gated on modern-only).

- **Tool description injection (CWE-20):** `_absorb_tool_listing()` validates `x-mcp-header` annotations and output schemas but never inspects `tool.description` — the field sent verbatim to the LLM context. Fix: regex scan against known prompt-injection patterns before pinning; drops tools that match on first sight.

- **DNS rebinding protection off by default (CWE-16):** `TransportSecurityMiddleware` defaulted to `enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False` for backwards compatibility. Fix: flip default to `True`; add a startup `WARNING` log when `allowed_hosts` is empty so misconfigured deployments fail visibly rather than silently rejecting all requests.

- **CWE-78 in CLI npx probe:** `subprocess.run([cmd, "--version"], shell=True)` on Windows. `cmd` is currently hardcoded, but `shell=True` with a list is exploitable if ever made configurable. Fix: remove `shell=True`.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mcp/client/session.py` | Add `_INJECTION_PATTERNS`, `_tool_desc_hash()`, `_scan_tool_description()`; security pass in `_absorb_tool_listing()` |
| `src/mcp/server/transport_security.py` | Flip DNS rebinding default to `True`; add empty-`allowed_hosts` startup warning |
| `src/mcp/cli/cli.py` | Remove `shell=True` from npx probe |

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing test suite: `pytest tests/client/ tests/transports/ tests/cli/` — 244 passed, 4 skipped (verified locally)
- [ ] `ruff check` on all three files — clean
- [ ] `pyright` on all three files — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [ ] New tests needed: rug-pull drop, injection drop, clean tool pass-through, legacy protocol also protected

## Background

These vectors were originally documented as part of the DEADBUG-MCP research series (rug-pull V3, cross-server poisoning V4). The rug-pull fix described by MCP Playground ("pin the tool definitions you approved, call the server several times, list again, and treat any difference as a security event") is now implemented at the SDK level in `_absorb_tool_listing()`.

Signed-off-by: Nicholas Michael Kloster <nicholas@nuclide-research.com>

Updates `black` from 26.3.1 to 26.10.1
Release notes

Sourced from black's releases.

26.10.1

Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This update is received automatically when using psf/black@stable, and is independent of the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from tool.black.required-version, it now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for black requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue has been registered as GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2; a CVE identifier is pending.

Stable style

  • Fix a long Jupyter notebook assignment magic (for example x = !ls -la) being wrapped in parentheses, which IPython can no longer run; such cells are now left unchanged (#5481)
  • Keep repeated lines outside the selected --line-ranges unchanged (#5436)
  • Fix --line-ranges formatting lines that follow a statement when formatting joins or re-indents that statement (#5484)
  • Fix --line-ranges crashing with an internal error when an unselected statement has a # fmt: skip comment on the last line before a closing bracket (#5477)
  • Prevent moving an encoding declaration (for example # -*- coding: latin-1 -*-) onto the first two lines of a file (#5487)
  • Fix adding an extra trailing blank line inside a multi-line module docstring when its last line is near the line length limit (#5494)

Preview style

  • Do not split short expressions on delimiters (such as binary operators, comparisons, or comprehensions) inside brackets when preceded by a standalone comment (#5455)
  • Fix the unstable string_processing feature removing backslash-newline sequences from raw strings, which changed their value (#5482)
  • Avoid adding unnecessary parentheses around unbreakable right-hand side expressions in assignments (such as annotated assignments or subscript targets) (#5473)
  • Parenthesize expressions with parameter comments when they exceed the line length under --preview (#5442)
  • Fix wrap_long_dict_values_in_parens dropping the parentheses around a right-hand side that contains a dictionary, leaving a line over the length limit (#5492)
  • Fix the unstable string_processing feature adding a space after * or ** in a PEP 695 type parameter (* Ts = ...) when it splits a string in the parameter's default (#5504)
  • Avoid unnecessary line splits of trailers (such as indexing/subscripts) when an earlier bracket split exceeds the line length only due to a trailing comment (#5498)

Configuration

  • Add --cache-dir to configure the cache directory from the command line (#5433)
  • Don't cache a file as formatted after formatting or checking it with --line-ranges,

title: Fix /token and /revoke OAuth error codes
body:
<!--
Pull requests from outside the maintainer team need to link an open issue that
a maintainer has assigned to you (or one labeled `help wanted`); others are
closed automatically until that's in place. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.
-->

Fixes #3723

`/token` and `/revoke` now use the error codes in [RFC 6749 §5.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-5.2). [RFC 7009 §2.2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009#section-2.2.1) reuses that presentation for revocation.

- A grant this server implements, but the client is not registered for, is `unauthorized_client`.
- A grant the server does not implement (`client_credentials`, `password`, or anything else outside `grant_types_supported`) is `unsupported_grant_type`, decided before the request union is validated, so the body is not a pydantic error.
- Failed client authentication on `/revoke` is `invalid_client`, the same code `/token` already returned.
- When that failure used `Authorization: Basic`, the 401 includes `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="OAuth"`. RFC 7617 §2 requires the realm on a Basic challenge. `client_secret_post` failures do not get the header, because the client did not use the Authorization field.

The jwt-bearer path no longer has a separate "grant disabled" branch. That grant is outside `grant_types_supported` unless identity assertion is enabled, so the early check already returns `unsupported_grant_type`.

## Motivation and Context

Clients that branch on these codes were reacting to the wrong condition. The two grant errors were swapped, `/revoke` still reported failed authentication as `unauthorized_client`, and a failed Basic authentication had no `WWW-Authenticate` header.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `uv run --frozen ruff check .` and `uv run --frozen ruff format --check .` are clean.
- `uv run --frozen pyright`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `./scripts/test`: 6223 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed, coverage 100%, strict-no-cover clean.
- New cases in `tests/server/auth/test_error_handling.py` cover the four rows in the issue. `test_client_without_the_grant_registered_is_rejected` now expects `unauthorized_client`.

## Breaking Changes

Successful token and revocation responses are unchanged. title: fix(server): answer unparseable stdio lines with a JSON-RPC error
body:
Fixes #2751

## Summary

When a stdio line fails message validation, the server now answers it on the wire with a JSON-RPC error frame instead of forwarding a bare exception on the read stream, which the server dispatcher drops. A request that cannot be parsed now completes instead of staying pending until the client times out.

## Motivation and Context

Reproduced on `main` (2af9e308) with `stdio_server()` over injected streams: a `ping` request with `params` nested to depth 256 fails validation with "Invalid JSON: recursion limit exceeded", arrives on the read stream as a bare exception, and nothing is written to stdout, so the request id never completes. A shallow ping right after it arrives fine, matching the report and the 2.3.0 confirmation on the issue. The Streamable HTTP transport already returns a `-32700` parse error for the same input; stdio did not.

The handling stays in the stdio transport, following the review direction on #2755 and #2766, rather than moving into the session or dispatcher layer:

- Invalid JSON gets `-32700` / "Parse error"; a line that parses but is not a valid message gets `-32600` / "Invalid request".
- The request id is recovered from the raw line where possible (a full parse first, then a pattern scan for lines too malformed to parse) and falls back to `id: null`, as JSON-RPC prescribes when the id cannot be determined.
- The error message is kept bare on purpose: the pydantic validation text embeds the offending input, which can be arbitrarily large.

One deliberate behaviour change: code reading `stdio_server()` streams directly no longer receives failed lines as in-stream exceptions. That is the path that made the bug possible, and the existing test for it has been updated to assert the error frame instead.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- New regression tests in `tests/server/test_stdio.py`, all failing on the unmodified code and passing with this change: the depth-256 request completes with a parse error carrying id 900256 while a following shallow ping still arrives; an end-to-end test through `MCPServer.run("stdio")` asserting the same on the real process streams; parametrized cases for id recovery (truncated JSON with string and numeric ids, no id, an unrecoverable id token) and for the invalid-request split.
- `tests/server/test_stdio.py`, `tests/client/test_stdio.py`, `tests/interaction/transports/test_stdio.py`, and `tests/server/test_lowlevel_exception_handling.py`: 64 passed.
- `src/mcp/server/stdio.py` coverage under those suites: 100%.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `pyright` on both changed files: clean.
- Full suite via `./scripts/test`: 6211 passed; the 12 failures (httpx `InvalidURL` cases, docs, a file-permission test) reproduce identically on unmodified `main` in this environment and are unrelated to this change.

## Breaking Changes

None for protocol clients: a request that previously hung now receives an error response. Direct consumers of the `stdio_server()` read stream no longer see failed lines as in-stream `Exception` items, as noted above.

title: fix(client): isolate HTTP read timeouts from sibling requests
body:
Related to #3560 (the HTTP ReadTimeout case). This does not fix every transport error in that issue.

Contain an HTTP read timeout in its request task and return a correlated `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (-32001), so one slow POST does not cancel sibling requests or tear down the shared session.

## Motivation and Context

With the current streamable HTTP transport, `httpx2.ReadTimeout` while awaiting POST response headers or reading a JSON response escapes into the shared AnyIO task group. Other in-flight calls are cancelled and transport cleanup raises an ExceptionGroup. This was observed downstream with MCP 2.3.0, FastMCP 4.1.1 and Cortex; the SDK-only regression tests reproduce it on main at 2af9e308.

The fix catches only ReadTimeout, resolves the original request through the existing response channel, and uses a fixed message rather than forwarding upstream exception details. No retry is added. Initial initialize/server-discover errors and explicit cancellation retain their existing behavior. Notification failures and other transport exception types remain outside this patch's scope.

This overlaps the ReadTimeout portion of #3584, which is closed and unmerged. This narrower patch uses REQUEST_TIMEOUT and also covers resumption-header timeouts.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- New regression scenarios cover response-header and JSON-body timeouts under legacy and 2026-07-28 protocols. Each keeps a sibling request in flight until the timeout reaches its caller, then verifies the sibling and a subsequent request succeed, with one submission per tool and a closed failed response body.
- Resumption GET timeout retains the original request ID and does not submit a POST retry.
- Handshake ReadTimeout remains a raw transport failure without starting a fallback handshake.
- A pinned-gap test records that a failed notification still ends the POST writer.
- All four primary scenarios fail against unpatched main with an escaping ReadTimeout.

Final validation (Python 3.12.15, upstream frozen lockfile):

- `./scripts/test` — 6,220 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed; 100% branch coverage; strict-no-cover passed.
- `uv run --frozen ruff check .` and formatting checks on changed Python files — passed.
- `uv run --frozen pyright src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py tests/client/test_streamable_http.py` — 0 errors.
- Full `uv run --frozen pyright` reports two macOS `os.waitid` errors in unchanged `tests/transports/stdio/test_lifecycle.py:190`; no errors in changed files.
- Downstream FastMCP/Cortex integration was not rerun for this upstream patch; those versions supplied the original report.

## Breaking Changes

A request-local HTTP ReadTimeout now reaches its caller as MCPError(REQUEST_TIMEOUT), rather than cancelling the surrounding task group and surfacing during transport cleanup. No public signatures or configuration change. Server execution may continue after the client's timeout; this fix does not make retrying mutating calls safe.

title: fix(prompts): await awaitable result returned by sync prompt callback (#3709)
body:
## Summary

Closes #3709.

When a synchronous prompt function returns an awaitable (coroutine, Task, or Future), `Prompt.render()` previously ran the sync callable in a worker thread via `anyio.to_thread.run_sync()`, but did not await the returned awaitable. This resulted in the coroutine object being serialized as fallback JSON/string representation:

```python
Left contains one more item: Message(role='user', content=TextContent(type='text', text='"<coroutine object ...>"'))
```

`PromptResult` explicitly allows `Awaitable[SyncPromptResult]`. This PR awaits any awaitable returned by the prompt callable before validating and converting messages.

## Root Cause

`Prompt.render()` ran `result = await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(...)` for non-async callables, but did not check `inspect.isawaitable(result)`.

## Fix

Added `if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result` immediately after running the prompt callable in `src/mcp/server/mcpserver/prompts/base.py`.

## Test Plan

- Added regression test `test_prompt_render_awaits_awaitable_returned_by_sync_callback` in `tests/server/mcpserver/prompts/test_base.py`.
- Verified test fails RED on base and passes GREEN with fix.
- Ran all 22 prompt tests in `test_base.py`: 22 passed.
